name: Megrez
description: A star 25 parsecs away, 2.1 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 59774: radius 2.123 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 23.146 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.3) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 59774: effective temperature 8694 +/- 1380 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.047)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 3.94 from 2024A&A...681A.107R; the 3 published values span log g 3.6 to 3.9433, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 59774: distance 24.685 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.004), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 25 parsecs away, 2.1 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 23 times the Sun's luminosity at 8,694 K, so 2.123 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 59774: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Megrez
quotes.card: Megrez, also called Delta Ursae Majoris, is a star in the northern constellation of Ursa Major.
quotes.introduction: With an apparent magnitude of +3.3, it is the dimmest of the seven stars in the Big Dipper asterism.
